Years passed, and the jars multiplied in quiet places—the mouth of a cave, the hollow of a tree, the lip of a well. Each coin asked nothing in return, only that mercy be given to another in turn. The river learned to forgive not by memory, but by the pattern of acts it witnessed: mercy begets mercy, and even a stubborn river can learn to forget its own hurt when love feeds it anew.
